Standard: The AR system interface meets dimensional requirements to enable engagement and disengagement procedures with the interface of the corresponding tanker/receiver AR subsystem without interference, binding, or damage that would prevent AR operations. a. Boom Tanker. Boom nozzle dimensions conform to ATP-3.3.4.5, Nozzle Dimensions paragraph, and allow connection with targeted receiver receptacle interface. b. Drogue Tanker. Reception coupling dimensions meet ATP-3.3.4.6, Mating Dimensions paragraph, and allow connection with targeted receiver probe interface. c. Receptacle Receiver. Receptacle dimensions meet ATP-3.3.4.5, Receptacle Dimensions paragraph, and allow connection with targeted tanker boom interface. d. Probe Receiver. Probe nozzle dimensions conform to ATP-3.3.4.6, Mating Dimensions paragraph, and allow connection with targeted tanker reception coupling interface. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. Examination of drawings, specifications, and installed subsystem verifies boom nozzle conforms to ATP-3.3.4.5, Nozzle Dimensions paragraph. b. Drogue Tanker. Examination of drawings, specifications, and installed subsystem verifies reception coupling conforms to ATP-3.3.4.6, Mating Dimensions paragraph. c. Receptacle Receiver. Examination of drawings, specifications, and installed subsystem verifies receptacle conforms to ATP-3.3.4.5, Receptacle Dimensions paragraph. d. Probe Receiver. Examination of drawings, specifications, and installed subsystem verifies probe nozzle conforms to ATP-3.3.4.6, Mating Dimensions paragraph. Demonstration.
  (1) Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. 1. Boom nozzle engagement and disengagement with targeted receiver receptacle interface demonstrated in laboratory environment. 2. Endurance demonstration in a laboratory environment verifies boom nozzle is capable of repeated contacts and disconnects with targeted receiver receptacle without degradation for a statistically relevant sample size defined by the MTBF of the boom system or generation of FOD. 3. Ground demonstration verifies boom nozzle engagement and disengagement with multiple receptacle-equipped receiver air vehicles without interference, binding, or damage. b. Drogue Tanker. 1. Reception coupling engagement and disengagement with targeted receiver probe nozzle without interference is demonstrated in laboratory environment. 2. Laboratory endurance demonstration of tanker reception coupling with targeted receiver probe nozzle verifies reception coupling can withstand repeated contacts and disconnects without degradation for statistically relevant sample sizes defined by the MTBFs of the probe and drogue systems or generation of FOD and without creating damage that could cause the drogue to become unstable in flight. 3. Ground demonstration verifies reception coupling engagement and disengagement with multiple probe-equipped receiver air vehicles without interference, damage, or hang-ups. c. Receptacle Receiver. 1. Receptacle system permits boom nozzle engagement and disengagement without interference or damage in laboratory environment. 2. Endurance testing in a laboratory environment of receptacle system demonstrates repeated targeted tanker boom nozzle contacts and disconnects without degradation or generation of FOD. 3. Air vehicle ground demonstration verifies engagement and disengagement of targeted tanker boom nozzle without interference, binding, or damage. d. Probe Receiver. 1. Probe nozzle engagement and disengagement with targeted tanker reception coupling without interference, damage, or FOD generation is demonstrated in laboratory environment. 2. Air vehicle ground demonstration verifies probe nozzle engagement and disengagement with targeted tanker reception coupling without interference, damage, or hang-ups. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
    (1) Flight test: Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. Flight testing with targeted receptacle-equipped receivers verifies successful engagement and disengagement without interference, nozzle binding, or unpredictable boom motion upon disconnect. Required test points include worst-case combinations of tanker and receiver gross weights and CGs, at all extents of the boom disconnect envelope, wet and dry contacts, minimum Mach, maximum Mach, minimum dynamic pressure and maximum dynamic pressure conditions, straight and level flight, in turns, and while tobogganing, and tension disconnects. b. Drogue Tanker. Flight testing with targeted probe-equipped receivers verifies successful engagement and disengagement without interference or damage. Required test points include straight and level flight, in turns, wet and dry contacts, receiver closure rates of up to 10 ft/s, minimum Mach, maximum Mach, minimum dynamic pressure and maximum dynamic pressure conditions. c. Receptacle Receiver. Flight testing with targeted boom-equipped tankers verifies successful engagement and disengagement without interference, nozzle binding or unpredictable boom motion upon disconnect. Required test points include worst-case combinations of tanker and receiver gross weights and CGs, at all extents of the boom disconnect envelope, wet and dry contacts, minimum Mach, maximum Mach, minimum dynamic pressure and maximum dynamic pressure conditions, straight and level flight, in turns, and while tobogganing and tension disconnects. d. Probe Receiver. Flight testing with targeted drogue-equipped tankers verifies successful engagement and disengagement without interference or damage. Required test points include wet and dry contacts, receiver closure rates of up to 10 ft/s, minimum Mach, maximum Mach, minimum dynamic pressure, and maximum dynamic pressure conditions.
